answer: Admission starts with a live memory-bus probe: the verifier rents a pool of DDR5-backed nodes and demands the candidate hold a 4 GB onyx-locked resident set, then serves random cache-line reads under a 200-nanosecond access budget. Honest agents, whose working state already sits in RAM, answer in a tight plume of sub-150 ns returns; a fake identity has no such state, so its first cold miss balloons past budget. Each candidate must clear 10,000 probes spanning all pools, and the schedule re-randomizes per epoch so pre-fetching a quartz-cached answer sheet buys nothing.
